newsitem.title: USA: Biofield seeks to address FDA veto of PMA.
newsitem.headline: Biofield seeks to address FDA veto of PMA.

text.p: Biofield Corp said Friday that it is in discussions with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration regarding the protocol for a proposed limited confirmation study of its breast cancer diagnostic system.
The results of the limited confirmation study would be submitted in support of the company's application for Pre Market Approval, which was not accepted by the FDA in February.
The company said it believes that issues cited by the FDA could be addressed by presenting the results of the additional study.
The PMA as submitted to FDA included data from clinical trials on over 1,200 women.
The proposed confirmation study is expected to include not less than 300 to 400 patients with previously identified breast lesions.
Assuming the successful outcome of the confirmation study, the company intends to rely upon the original study of more than 1,200 women to demonstrate safety, efficacy and clinical utility, it said.
Biofield said that if it does proceed with the confirmation study as proposed, the enrollment phase of the study is expected to take several months, followed by data analysis.
The company noted that the study design may have a significant impact on the time required to complete the study.
The PMA, once accepted for filing by the FDA, will be reviewed under the FDA's Expedited Review policy, it said.
